validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence, classification, or duplicate status. Length and diameter are well-corroborated; see the separate spec flags below for StartYear1, Capacity and SegmentCost.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + ROUTE: confirmed independently of GEM/gem.wiki by TWO primary sources I read directly (not just cited by the wiki page). (1) Naftogaz's own 'Master Plan. Ukrainian Gas Transmission System (UGTS). Priority Objects. Modernisation and Reconstruction' (2009, hosted by the Energy Charter Secretariat) names 'Ananiiv-Tyraspil-Izmail' explicitly as one of the two named lines of the 'South transit corridor' (the other being Yelets-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih / GEM P0783), maps its route through Ananiiv -> (Moldova) -> Tyraspil -> Izmail with a dedicated slide ('Modernisation and Reconstruction of South Transit Corridor', combined finance expenditure $366.3m for both lines). (2) KPMG's 'Situation of the Ukrainian natural gas market and transit system' (Oct 2017, prepared for Nord Stream 2 AG; the origin domain nord-stream2.com no longer resolves, so I cite the Internet Archive snapshot) lists 'Ananjiv-Tiraspol-Izmail' as item (15) of Ukraine's 15 named main transmission pipelines, in its own row of a technical-characteristics table (age, length, diameter, pressure, book value) sourced to 'Ukrtransgaz Annual Report 2015, Naftogaz Annual Report 2015, Report on the evaluation of assets BT 2012'. Both sources are independent of each other, of gem.wiki, and of GEM. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as a gas transmission trunk (not a gathering/feeder line) -- KPMG groups it with the other 14 named main transmission trunks, all 1.2-1.4m diameter, 5.5-7.5 MPa pressure-class lines. DUPLICATE CHECK against the roster's 'Izmail corridor' / 'Ananiiv hub' clusters flagged in the scope guidance: en.wikipedia.org's 'Natural gas in Ukraine' article states outright (citing a 2012 Ministry of Energy/Energy Community filing) that 'Main pipelines of the southern transit corridor are the Yelets-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih pipeline [P0783], the Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Rozdilna-Izmail pipeline [P0784], the Kremenchuk-Ananyiv-Bohorodchany pipeline [P1485], the Ananyiv-Tiraspol-Izmail pipeline [THIS ROW, P0786], and the Rozdilna-Izmail pipeline [P0787]' -- five distinct, separately named physical trunks, matching the roster 1:1 by name. This pipeline is further distinguished operationally: per the same Wikipedia article, it is the ONLY one of the five that crosses into Moldova/Transnistria proper (entering at the Hrebenyky gas metering station and re-entering Ukraine before Izmail), whereas P0784 and P0787 enter/exit via the separate Ryasnopil (Rozdilna) metering station and stay on Ukrainian territory. So P0786 is not a relabel or segment double-count of P0783/P0784/P1485/P0787 -- it is the one line in the cluster with a genuinely different (cross-border-via-Moldova) routing, confirmed by two independent primary corridor-planning documents plus a tertiary cross-check. Not independently re-verified: the Wikipedia claim is itself useful corroboration but I treat the two primary documents (Naftogaz Master Plan 2009 + KPMG 2017) as the load-bearing sources.

validity.recommendation: No change to Owner1. Suitable for the Owner [ref] cell on the operators_owners tab.
validity.researcher_notes: ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' at 100% is CORRECT and matches this country's post-2020 unbundling reality (per the scope guidance: since 1 Jan 2020 the state-owned Gas TSO of Ukraine, not the old Ukrtransgaz and NOT Gazprom, holds/operates the domestic GTS). Confirmed by two sources independent of each other and of gem.wiki: (1) the UN Global Compact's participant registry lists the legal entity 'Limited Liability Company \"Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine\"' by that exact name; (2) ENTSOG's own members/observers page names Ukraine's observer TSO as 'LLC Gas TSO of Ukraine'. This is a wholly-domestic Ukrainian trunk (does not cross into Russia/Belarus), so the Gazprom-ownership trap described in the scope guidance does not apply here -- and correctly, GEM does not show Gazprom as an owner on this row.

validity.recommendation: Do not treat StartYear1=1968 as settled. Recommend Update chase Ukrtransgaz's/Naftogaz's own asset/technical passport for a primary commissioning date -- I found two independent-of-each-other alternate dates, neither of which I could fully verify to Update's bar, but both disagree with 1968.
validity.researcher_notes: StartYear1=1968 is not corroborated by anything I found, and two separate leads point elsewhere. (1) KPMG's 2017 technical-characteristics table gives this pipeline's 'Age' as 46 years -- i.e. implies commissioning ~1971, not 1968. I sanity-checked this 'age' column's reliability against a pipeline with an independently known date: the same table's Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod row gives age=33 (implying 1984), which matches en.wikipedia's confirmed 1984 UPU commissioning date exactly -- so the KPMG age figures are a validated proxy for true commissioning year, not noise. That puts Ananjiv-Tiraspol-Izmail's likely build year at ~1971, a 3-year disagreement with the sheet. (2) Separately, en.wikipedia.org's 'Natural gas in Ukraine' article states 'Between 1986 and 2001, the Yelets-Kremenchuk-Ananyiv-Tiraspol-Izmail route was developed', citing a 2011 Ukrtransgaz presentation ('Ukrainian Gas Transmission System (UGTS). Modernisation and Reconstruction', The Energy Exchange) that is now a dead link I could not reach by any route to verify directly -- so I am NOT proposing this as a ref, only flagging it as a second, independent-sounding claim that disagrees with 1968 by a much larger margin (and does not fully agree with the KPMG-implied ~1971 either). I am not proposing a replacement StartYear because my two leads disagree with each other as much as they disagree with GEM -- this needs a primary Ukrtransgaz source, not adjudication by me.

validity.recommendation: Leave Capacity=23.70 bcm/y as-is (plausible, in the right range for a 1200mm/5.5MPa trunk) but do not treat it as independently corroborated. Recommend Update search Naftogaz's own technical passport or an ENTSOG capacity filing for a primary figure.
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity=23.70 bcm/y appears on gem.wiki (sourced there only to the same KPMG report I already read directly) and is repeated verbatim on en.wikipedia.org -- but I could not find this specific number anywhere in the actual KPMG 2017 PDF text (I downloaded and ran pdftotext -layout on the full document; it contains no '23.7' associated with this pipeline -- the only '23.7' figures in that PDF are unrelated annual financing amounts in mln USD for an entry-point metering-station project). Nor does the Naftogaz Master Plan (2009) document give a bcm/year figure for this specific line (it gives combined-project financing, not per-line throughput). So this number, while plausible, currently traces to gem.wiki/Wikipedia only as far as I can independently confirm -- not to a primary document I could read myself. Flagging as an uncorroborated (not necessarily wrong) spec point rather than silently passing it.

validity.recommendation: Flag for Update review: SegmentCost=$40,000,000 likely conflates 'construction cost' with 'net book value'. Recommend either leaving as a rough proxy with a ResearcherNotes caveat, or blanking it pending a real original-construction-cost source.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's SegmentCost=$40,000,000 (USD, no year given) is suspiciously close to a DIFFERENT figure I found in KPMG's 2017 table: this pipeline's 2017 net book value (NBV) is listed as $41 million. Net book value is the current depreciated accounting value of an asset already ~46 years old in 2017 -- it is not the same concept as an original construction/segment cost, and would not be expected to closely track a 1968-vintage Soviet pipeline's real build cost after decades of depreciation. gem.wiki's own page text states 'the net book value of the pipeline is US$41 million', sourced to the same KPMG report. This strongly suggests GEM's SegmentCost field is a repurposed net-book-value figure mislabeled as construction cost, not an actual build-cost figure (and the sheet is not even citing the year the $41M NBV applies to, 2017, which underscores that it is not a construction-cost figure). I am not proposing $41M as a fix (it is not the right concept for SegmentCost either) -- just flagging that the current value's provenance looks like a category error.

fills.researcher_notes: Status is inferable from context, not a literal token. KPMG's 2017 table records current net book value, age, and technical parameters for this pipeline as one of Ukraine's 15 active main transmission trunks (not a decommissioned/retired asset); Naftogaz's 2009 Master Plan describes it as a live modernization/reconstruction target within the operating South Transit Corridor. Neither source describes the line as out of service. Per the country-scope guidance, the 2025-01-01 end of Gazprom transit through Ukraine is not evidence this domestic-corridor trunk went offline -- I found no dated evidence this specific line was taken out of service, and it plays no role in Russian transit (its Moldova crossing near Tiraspol is unrelated to the Sudzha/Sokhranivka entry-point transit route). url_verifier's content check FAILed on the Wayback/KPMG PDF (large-PDF extraction-depth limitation documented in url_verifier.py's own docstring); I manually confirmed the relevant table row via pdftotext -layout ('Ananjiv-Tiraspol-Izmail ... 46 257 41 142 433 ... 1.2 3 5.5').
Both sources describe this as part of the Ukrainian NATURAL GAS transmission/transit system throughout; trivial fuel confirmation.

Not adding a ref: I could not corroborate 1968, and what I did find disagrees with it (see the StartYear spec concern in validity[] -- KPMG's age-derived ~1971, and an unverifiable-but-noted Wikipedia claim of 1986-2001 sourced to a dead Ukrtransgaz 2011 link). Declining to fabricate support for an unconfirmed value; flagged for Update to chase a primary Ukrtransgaz/Naftogaz record instead.

See the Capacity spec concern in validity[]: I read the full KPMG 2017 PDF text directly and did not find a '23.7' figure tied to this pipeline (only unrelated financing amounts elsewhere in the same document). No independent primary source found for this number in this pass; not proposing a ref rather than reusing gem.wiki/Wikipedia's unsourced-to-me figure.

KPMG's 2017 technical-characteristics table gives this pipeline's diameter as 1.2m = exactly 1200mm, matching GEM precisely. Only one primary source found with an exact figure (tier=medium per the corroboration rule -- one strong source). url_verifier's automated content check FAILed on this large PDF (documented extraction-depth limitation); manually confirmed via pdftotext -layout: row reads 'Ananjiv-Tiraspol-Izmail ... 46 257 41 142 433 ... 1.2 3 5.5' where the trailing '1.2' is the Diameter(m)/'3' is CS count/'5.5' is working pressure (MPa) column, matching the table's legend and cross-checked against neighboring rows whose diameters I could independently confirm (e.g. UPU's own '1.4' = 1400mm matches GEM's own multi-value diameter for P0768).

KPMG's 2017 table gives length=257km exactly matching GEM. One primary source with an exact match (tier=medium). en.wikipedia.org's 'Natural gas in Ukraine' article separately states '256 kilometres (159 mi)' for this pipeline -- a 1km / 0.4% difference from GEM/KPMG, not material, likely rounding; noting it rather than treating it as a second independent corroboration (Wikipedia's own citation for that figure traces to a source I could not verify, per the Capacity/StartYear notes above, so I am not counting it as confirming). url_verifier content check FAILed on this large PDF (documented limitation, see Diameter note above); manually confirmed via pdftotext -layout.

EndLocation='Izmail'/EndCountryOrArea='Ukraine' (already on sheet) confirmed by both the Naftogaz Master Plan map and KPMG's route table -- high tier, 2 independent sources. StartLocation was BLANK on the sheet -- deep-filled as 'Anan'iv' (the pipeline's own name-eponymous origin town, shown as the route's Ukrainian starting point on the Naftogaz Master Plan's South-corridor map, before the line crosses into Moldova via Tiraspol and back into Ukraine to Izmail). StartState/Province and EndState/Province were both blank -- filled as 'Odesa Oblast' for both ends: en.wikipedia.org confirms Izmail is 'a city ... in Odesa Oblast', and separately confirms Anan'iv (Ananiv) 'is a city of Podilsk Raion in Odesa Oblast, Ukraine'. Left StartPrefecture/District and EndPrefecture/District blank rather than force a raion-level claim I can't tie precisely to the pipeline's own start point (a rural corridor, not necessarily coincident with the town's own raion boundary).

Not adding a ref: see the SegmentCost spec concern in validity[]. The $40M figure looks like a mislabeled net-book-value number (KPMG's actual 2017 NBV for this pipeline is $41M, a different concept than original construction/segment cost for a 1968-vintage asset), and I found no primary source stating an actual construction cost. Declining to cite a source that would misrepresent what it actually supports.

summary: P0786 (Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail): existence, route, transmission classification, non-duplicate status vs. the Izmail-corridor cluster (P0783/P0784/P1485/P0787), and Owner attribution all CONFIRMED via 2 independent primary/authoritative sources each; Length (257km) and Diameter (1200mm) confirmed exact-match via one primary source (KPMG 2017) at medium tier. THREE spec concerns flagged: StartYear1=1968 conflicts with a KPMG-age-derived ~1971 AND an unverifiable Wikipedia claim of 1986-2001 (neither resolved, no replacement proposed); Capacity=23.7 bcm/y is uncorroborated by any primary source I could read; SegmentCost=$40M looks like a mislabeled net-book-value figure (KPMG's actual 2017 NBV is $41M), not a real construction cost. Deep-filled a blank StartLocation (Anan'iv) and both State/Province fields (Odesa Oblast) with verified refs.
